text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- The defence ministry to revise the invalid status of some 20,000 Croatian veterans of the 1991-95 war.
- An announced four-hour warning strike of the education, science and social welfare employees is on, following a failure of talks over a pay rise with the government.
- November wholesale prices of industrial products up 0.5 percent from October, 2.3 percent year-on-year.

- Croatian PM's proposed cabinet reshuffle approved by President Tudjman: Ivan Penic, former privatisation minister, to replace interior minister Ivan Jarnjak who becomes the head of the National Security Office. Milan Kovac becomes privatisation minister and Marko Sirac construction minister.

- Tapping of regular phones, cellular phones, faxes and computers only to be possible with a court order, according to the draft penal code changes. A six-hour police detention will have to be followed by either pressing of charges or release.
- Interview with education and sports minister Ljilja Vokic: The teachers' strike will not resolve anything.
- The war has produced some 100,000 alcoholics, says in an interview physician Darko Breitenfeld, expert on the subject. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
